Test image shows a mango leaf with distinct dark brown/black irregular spots scattered across an otherwise green leaf. The spots are discrete, roughly circular to irregular in shape, with defined edges. No white powder, no sooty coating, no tip dieback pattern.

Now I'll view one reference from each class.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Healthy green mango leaf with 4-5 discrete, well-defined dark brown/black spots scattered across the blade. No powder, no sooty coating, no tip necrosis.
- **Anthracnose ref**: Advanced necrotic/yellowed leaf — consistent with the same disease progressing from isolated spots.
- **Die_Back ref**: Completely shriveled brown stem/tissue — clearly different.
- **Powdery_Mildew ref**: Diffuse white powdery coating all over — does not match discrete dark spots.
- **Sooty_Mould ref**: Dark sooty smear/coating covering large areas — more diffuse, not discrete spots.

The discrete, well-defined dark lesions on an otherwise green leaf are characteristic of early **Anthracnose**, which causes isolated necrotic spots before progressing to full leaf blight.
